Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Energy Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Energy Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Operating Officer; Elena Vasquez, VP of Exploration; and David Chen, VP of Marketing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Nexus Energy delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust production growth averaging over 110,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, with meaningful quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year gains in both oil and gas volumes. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on emissions reduction targets as part of our ESG initiatives. We are focused on capital discipline, coming in under budget on key areas like drilling and facilities while navigating some completion cost pressures. Further, we are working on cost reduction efforts that have driven lifting costs to competitive lows. We continue to adjust to market dynamics in refining with strong throughput and margins. Finally, we are taking steps to strengthen our balance sheet through proactive debt management.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.5 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $800 million, and net income was $550 million. We generated $600 million in free cash flow and returned $300 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $14.2 billion in total debt, net debt at $11.8 billion, and $2.4 billion in cash.

Let me provide more color on our capital discipline with a detailed walkthrough of our capex breakdown across drilling, completion, and facilities—budget versus actual through the first nine months of 2024. Our full-year guidance remains at $1.6 to $1.7 billion, reflecting our disciplined approach to high-return development primarily in the Permian Basin, where we hold over 1.2 million net acres of Tier 1 inventory, supplemented by selective activity in the Eagle Ford and Bakken.

Nine-month total capex stands at $1.18 billion, approximately 4% below our $1.23 billion pro-rata budget. This underspend stems from operational efficiencies and supply chain optimizations, partially offset by inflationary pressures in proppant and completion services. We've kept our rig count at an average of 12 operated rigs—eight in the Delaware Basin and four in the Midland—while turning to sales 22 wells in Q3 alone.

Drilling capex came in at $498 million against a $520 million budget, 4% under. This was due to enhanced drilling efficiencies from using high-spec Cat 1250 rigs from Nabors and Precision Drilling, equipped with our proprietary automation suites. Average drilling days per 10,000-foot lateral dropped to 14.2 days from 16.1 days in Q3 2023—a 12% improvement—thanks to optimized bottom-hole assemblies with 8-blade PDC bits from Halliburton and real-time geosteering via our partnership with SLB's DrillOps on Demand.

In the Delaware Basin's Northern Shelf, targeting the Wolfcamp A and B benches, we spudded 28 wells against a budget of 30, but curve-to-total depth ratios improved to 98.5%, minimizing doglegs and non-productive time. Midland activity focused on the Lower Spraberry, with 18 spuds benefiting from pad drilling synergies that reduced mobilization costs by 15%. Bakken drilling was lighter at $45 million actual versus $50 million budgeted, as we deferred two pads amid softer local oil realizations around $72 per barrel WTI equivalent.

This underspend allows us to pull forward Q4 drilling without incremental spend, supporting our goal of 95 gross wells turned-to-flow by year-end.

Completion capex was $472 million against $450 million budgeted, 5% over due to transient cost inflation, but we've clawed back momentum. This overrun of $22 million was driven by a 10% year-over-year rise in proppant pricing—our average landed cost hit $65 per ton for 100-mesh sand from Hi-Crush and Badger Mining—coupled with zipper frac scheduling across 10-well pads in the Delaware. Proppant intensity averaged 2,500 pounds per foot, with slickwater designs incorporating diverter tech from Liberty Energy to boost cluster efficiency to 85%.

We're rolling out our MaxConnect completion methodology, tailored to our hybrid fluid systems: 65% water, 20% linear gel, and 15% specialty chemistry from ChampionX. This has lifted 30-day initial production rates to 1,400 BOE per day per well in the Wolfcamp C, a 15% uplift over 2023 vintages. Eagle Ford completions, at $65 million actual versus $60 million budget, saw higher fluid costs from regional water sourcing amid Texas drought premiums, but our recycle rate exceeded 75%, mitigating impacts.

We've locked in Q4 contracts at flat pricing, expecting to end the year at budget through cadence optimization—18 turn-in-lines planned for Q4.

Facilities capex was $210 million against $260 million budgeted, 19% under by $50 million, reflecting smart modularization and deferred non-core builds. Spend focused on centralized oil treating and gas compression: we commissioned two 20,000 barrel per day separators in Midland using prefabricated skids from EnerFlex, cutting install time by 40% and capex by 25% per unit versus stick-built.

In the Delaware, our $85 million on water management—midstream tie-ins to WTG Midstream's system—yielded a 22% underspend through negotiated compression rates at $0.15 per MMBtu. Bakken facilities were minimal at $20 million, prioritizing lease automation over new infrastructure. This discipline follows our Facilities Lite strategy: 80% of new pads now connect to existing infrastructure within 5 miles, slashing takeaway bottlenecks.

The variance here directly funds our $200 million share repurchase authorization, enhancing shareholder returns amid WTI at $78 per barrel.

Overall, these variances underscore our capex agility: 70% of spend now yields over 60% internal rate of return at $65 per barrel, with Permian inventory supporting 10+ years at current pace. Cost deflation trends persist—service intensity down 8% year-over-year—bolstered by LNG export demand curbing gas flaring fines. Risks include helical pile delays in facilities and potential rig rate hikes if steel tariffs bite, but our frame agreements with Patterson-UTI cap exposure.

For Q4, we anticipate $400-450 million spend, landing full-year at the low end of guidance. This funds 92-98 gross turn-in-lines, positioning us for 75,000-80,000 BOE per day production exit rate.

Shifting to our balance sheet strength, particularly our debt profile, which continues to underscore our financial discipline amid a volatile macro environment. With WTI averaging $82 per barrel and Brent at $86 through the quarter—buoyed by OPEC+ cuts and resilient global demand—our upstream operations generated robust free cash flow, enabling us to meaningfully deleverage while advancing our high-return inventory.

Total debt stood at $14.2 billion as of September 30, a $1.8 billion reduction from $16.0 billion at year-end 2023 and down 12% quarter-over-quarter. This reflects strategic repayments and refinancing activity. Short-term debt is minimal at $450 million, primarily revolving credit draws that we fully repaid post-quarter end using excess cash. Our long-term debt portfolio is investment-grade rated—BBB- from S&P and Baa3 from Moody's—and maturity laddered out to 2035, with no major walls before 2026.

Cash and equivalents ended at $2.4 billion, up from Q2, with $1.5 billion undrawn on our $5 billion syndicated revolver backed by JPMorgan and Citi. Net debt is $11.8 billion, a 22% year-over-year decline from prior peaks and our lowest since pre-COVID.

Leverage ratios improved sharply: net debt to trailing twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA at 1.3x—a 35% reduction from 2.0x at year-end 2023 and below our 1.5x target. This is ahead of peers like Occidental at 1.8x and ConocoPhillips at 1.4x. Gross debt to EBITDA is 1.6x, debt-to-capitalization at 28%, down from 35% last year.

Deleveraging is driven by cash flow from core basins. In the Permian, with 450,000 net acres and 180,000 BOE per day pumped in Q3 up 15% year-over-year, we've captured full-cycle returns exceeding 50% using our proprietary ApexFlow hydraulic fracturing tech—longer laterals averaging 12,000 feet with enhanced proppant intensity. This generated substantial Permian FCF directed toward retiring a $1 billion term loan.

Eagle Ford and Bakken held steady at 90,000 BOE per day combined, with low-breakeven assets under $40 WTI. Gulf of Mexico deepwater, highlighted by King's Quay FPSO ramping to 85,000 BOE per day gross, contributed meaningfully, funding paydown on export facility debt. We've hedged 65% of 2024 oil at $75 per barrel floors.

Strategically, we're returns-driven. Post-quarter, we launched a $500 million tender for 5.875% senior notes due 2027, replacing with 4.75% green bonds tied to Scope 1 reductions from electrified rigs, shaving 50-75 basis points off our 4.8% all-in cost. Executed $800 million in divestitures YTD, proceeds to debt—no creep.

Forward, Q4 FCF targets net debt under $11 billion and leverage below 1.2x, supporting dividend hikes yielding 3.2% and $2 billion repurchases, 15 million shares retired at $95 average.

Now, on lifting costs per BOE—a key metric underscoring our operational excellence and free cash flow generation even in volatility. Lifting costs, or lease operating expenses, represent cash costs to produce and maintain assets per BOE, excluding exploration, development, and non-cash items.

Company-wide, we hit $11.20 per BOE in Q3, a 17% year-over-year decline from $13.50 and 4% sequential improvement from Q1. This is our 10th straight quarter of reductions, trailing 12-month average $11.80—below peer median $14.50 per S&P Global, competitive with Pioneer and EOG.

Over time, costs have fallen 28% from $15.60 post-pandemic peak in 2021, via scale, tech, and gating. Progression shows consistent declines despite labor and tubular inflation eased to +8% year-over-year per EIA.

Regionally, Permian (65% production) dropped to $8.75 per BOE, 22% year-over-year, via horizontal efficiencies and water management—rivaling Occidental sub-$9. Bakken at $14.20 down 12%, offset by emulsion optimizations. Gulf of Mexico to $18.40 from $21.50, 14% decline on FPSO uptime over 98%. North Sea to $22.10, ring-fenced at under 5% production.

These stem from a $250 million 2024 program targeting 20-25% reductions versus 2023. Digital and automation (35% savings): Schlumberger Delfi on 80% Permian pads for AI maintenance, cutting downtime 25%; Baker Hughes robotic pumps on 40% Bakken, saving $150k per pull; IoT for $0.75 per BOE power savings.

Chemical and water (25%): Nalco nanoparticle polymers cut chemicals 18% to $1.20 per BOE; Permian ZLD processes 60% water, disposal from $1.50 to $0.85 per barrel on 8:1 cuts.

Supply chain (20%): Locked tubulars, Halliburton sand logistics 12% freight savings, diesel hedged at $2.80 gallon.

Labor (15%): ROCs cut headcount 18%, TRIR 0.12, bonuses tied to LOE.

Asset sales (5%): $150 million North Sea exit, reallocating to sub-$10 Permian.

This fortifies us—$1.2 billion Q2 FCF at $80 WTI, breakeven $25 per BOE all-in. Target $10.50 Q4, sub-$10 2025; GoM electrification another $1.00 by 2026.

Turning to refining, which delivered robust performance. Adjusted EBITDA $1.2 billion, up 25% year-over-year and 15% sequential, on high cracks, throughput, efficiency.

Throughput averaged 1.45 million barrels per day, 96% utilization—top peer, over Valero 94%, Marathon 93%. Up 5% quarter-over-quarter from 1.38 million, 12% year-over-year from 1.29 million, on demand unwind.

USGC Port Arthur/Lake Charles 1.05 million at 98%, heavy WTI Midland/Eagle Ford sours 28 API 1.2% sulfur. Midwest Whiting 285,000 at 95%, PADD 2 distillates $22 per barrel. West Coast El Segundo 115,000 at 92%, CARB offset by RBOB. Q3 steady 1.4-1.5 million, Q4 97% post-turnaround.

Margins $18.50 per barrel, up 18% quarter-over-quarter, 30% year-over-year. 3:2:1 $16.80 USGC, $19.20 Midwest, $14.50 West—over NYMEX $15.10. NCI 12.2, clean yields 88% up 2 points, 52% distillates vs peer 48%.

Distillate $25 ULSD, gasoline $12 RBOB. Hedged 60% Q3 at $17. Edge from coking 25%, hydrocracking on Canadian heavies vs Phillips 66 $14.80.

Efficiency: cash costs $4.20 per barrel, 8% down, EBITDA $8.30 up from $6.50. Energy 85,000 BTU down 5% on $150 million program—VSDs, AI FCC. Maintenance $220 million.

Yields: distillate 52% via alkylation debottlenecks $2 value. Renewables: 10,000 barrel per day Whiting unit for RD, IRA credits, 15% PADD 2 by 2026.

Strategically, 2.0 million capacity 75% high-NCI for distillate supercycle. $500 million Port Arthur coker +20,000 by 2026 on Permian sours. Path to Zero CCUS 1.5 million tons by 2027.

Risks hurricanes, Asia capacity; advantages shale proximity, 2.5x debt/EBITDA. FY2024 EBITDA $5.0-5.5 billion, $12-14 margins 94%.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Torres for an operational update.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 110,500 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Permian Delaware Basin wells online, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives across basins.

Now I will turn it over to Elena Vasquez for an update on our exploration activities.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill five exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Finally, I'll turn it over to David Chen to discuss our marketing strategy.

David Chen: Thank you, Elena. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for refined products in the US Gulf Coast, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen relationships with existing customers. The impact on our margins from high distillate cracks and clean yields has been significant.

Sarah Jenkins: Before we open the line for Q&A, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our ESG initiatives, focusing on emissions reduction targets—a core pillar of our sustainability strategy at Nexus Energy Inc. We've committed to net-zero Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 2035 across operated assets, with Scope 3 aligned to the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C pathway by 2050. This drives value through efficiency, risk mitigation, and leadership in energy transition.

In Q3 2024, we achieved a 28% year-over-year reduction in consolidated Scope 1 and 2 emissions intensity to 18.2 kg CO2e per BOE—well ahead of our 2025 target of 22 kg and on track for 2030's 12 kg.

Total Scope 1 and 2 emissions fell 15% quarter-over-quarter to 4.2 million metric tons CO2e, from production efficiency and abatement projects. Upstream (72% footprint) saw steep declines, flaring intensity to 0.8% of gross gas—down from 1.2% year ago, per World Bank Zero Routine Flaring pledge. Methane intensity to 0.22 kg CH4/BOE, 35% reduction year-over-year, surpassing OGMP 2.0 Gold Standard—50% below Permian average 0.45 kg per EPA.

Scope 2 down 22% to 450,000 tons from 65% renewable U.S. sourcing via NextEra and Ørsted PPAs. Scope 3 ~85% from sold products, now granular per Oil and Gas GHG Protocol, TCFD disclosures.

Invested $450 million year-to-date in abatement, 3.2x ROI via fees, credits, opex savings. Key programs: Methane suite with FLIR drones, Seekir satellites on 85% assets, 1,200+ leaks fixed averting 45,000 tons; Permian pneumatic replacements with Chart zero-emission actuators, 42% fugitive cut.

Flaring/venting: Bakken VRUs capture 98% associated gas up from 82%; two midstream electrification with CAT generators, 60,000 MMBtu diesel reduction.

Electrification: 45% rigs electrified via Nabors, SLB VoltH2S, 30% Scope 1 NOx/CO2 per well cut; VFDs, efficient motors in 120+ compressors, 18% energy savings like Chevron Delfin.

CCUS: Permian Nexus Hub JV with Occidental, Denbury sequestered 1.1 million tons at $25/ton, 45Q credit; Phase 2 FID Q2 2025 for 5 MMtpa 2030; Eagle Ford blue H2 pilot with Air Products.

Aligns IPIECA, S&P CSA score 72/100 up 15 points.

Regional: Permian (42% prod) intensity down 32% to 15.5 kg, $250M pipe-to-well like EQT; flaring 0.5 Bcf down 55% despite 12% prod growth to 450 Mbbl/d, Texas HB 40 tailwinds.

Bakken (18%) methane 40% cut to 0.18 kg via LDAR, electrified fracs.

North Sea (15%) Scope 1 down 25% to 10.8 kg, Troll Phase 3 grid-tied like Equinor; Sverdrup P&A ahead to 2026.

Middle East JVs (15%) ADNOC 22% flaring via Ruwais CCUS; QatarEnergy LNG 20% below global average.

Guyana baseline-zero electrified.

ESG embedded—15% of 2025 $4.2B upstream ($630M). De-risks EU CBAM, SEC rules; $150M annual California LCFS credits. Abatement $12/ton from $18, EU ETS competitive.

Q4 10-12% intensity cut, full-year 25% below 2023. Risks VFD delays, Waha constraints; offsets LNG (15% below JKM), SAF with United, refinery biofuels.

Our trajectory validates low-cost, low-carbon ops—18% ROCE on ESG, thriving in $80-90/bbl IEA Stated Policies.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Brian Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on your overall strategy amid energy transition pressures?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, Brian. Absolutely. Our strategy centers on high-return inventory in top-tier basins like the Permian, paired with aggressive ESG execution to lower our carbon profile ahead of peers. We're generating strong free cash flow to deleverage and return capital, while investing in CCUS and electrification for long-term resilience. This positions us to deliver value regardless of price decks or policy shifts.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Ramirez with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez: Good morning. What are your expectations for production volumes, total, oil, gas—quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year?

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, John. Great question on production volumes—always a key focus for us here at Nexus Energy. Let me walk you through our Q3 2024 results in detail, with breakdowns on total BOE per day, oil, and natural gas, including quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year comps. I'll tie this into drivers, regional performance, and forward outlook.

Headline: Q3 averaged 110,500 BOE per day, +5.2% quarter-over-quarter from 105,000 in Q2 and +16.3% year-over-year from 95,000 in Q3 2023. On pace for full-year midpoint 115,000 BOE per day amid WTI $81 average, Henry Hub $2.70.

By commodity: Oil 71,200 barrels per day, +7.1% quarter-over-quarter from 66,500, +21.4% year-over-year from 58,600—64% of total, up from 61%. Natural gas 233 MMcf per day or 38,800 BOE equivalent (6:1), flat quarter-over-quarter but +3.8% year-over-year; 36% mix. NGLs steady 1,500 barrels per day, 1%.

Quarter-over-quarter uplift from Q2 completions: 28 gross (22.4 net) operated Delaware wells, 45-day IPs 1,850 BOE per day 75% oil—12% over type curve on 12,500-foot laterals, ceramic proppants boosting EUR 15-20%. Permian drove +4,800 BOE per day net, 92% of beat.

Offset base declines -2,100 BOE per day Eagle Ford/Bakken (25-30% annualized), mitigated by 12 workover rigs adding 800 BOE per day via plunger lifts, acid stims. Bakken weather -300 early, 90% recovered.

Regional: Permian 72% at 79,500 BOE per day +6.8% quarter-over-quarter / +22% year-over-year; Delaware pads adjacent Occidental, Second Bone Spring connectivity managed.

Eagle Ford 18% 19,800 +2.1% / +9%; Pearsall oil cuts 65%.

Bakken 8% 8,800 -1.2% / +5%; post-divestiture, high-GOR focus.

Gulf of Mexico 2% 2,400 flat; stable Mars upgrades.

Year-over-year from 2023 bolt-ons $450 million 12,000 Permian acres +8,500 annualized. AI frac with Halliburton 25-foot spacing, 18% productivity; D&C $850/foot down 11%.

55% 2024 capex deployed $675 million of $1.2 billion, reaffirming oil to 75,000 by year-end, 60% Q4 hedged $78. Gas mid-single growth to LNG. Risks OPEC to $75 accelerating deflation; upside 15 DUCs Q4.

John, does that cover it, or zoom in on Permian DD&A?

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Could you please provide more color on operational efficiencies in the basins?

Michael Torres: Thanks, Lisa. Our efficiencies are shining through lower drilling days, higher cluster efficiency in completions, and water management tying into midstream. In Permian, pad synergies and automation have cut costs while boosting IPs. Base decline management with workovers keeps us flat on legacy assets, and we're applying digital tools across to sustain momentum into 2025.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Patel: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Elena Vasquez: Good question, Mark. The Permian seismic has identified high-potential Wolfcamp extensions, and our five planned wells could add multi-year inventory at low risk. Success here extends our Tier 1 runway beyond 10 years, allowing sustained activity at current paces without chasing marginal plays—keeping returns high and capex focused.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: What is the outlook for refined products in the coming years?

David Chen: Morning, Rachel. Strong, with distillate supercycle tailwinds through 2025 per IEA. We're expanding USGC offtake, leveraging high yields and hedging to capture cracks. Renewables ramp positions us for premium RD volumes, and CCUS enhances product slate for compliant markets—expecting steady EBITDA growth at 94-96% utilization.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
